First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}-y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y) \\  & =2y-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2y-1}.
$$
